factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit EUR 24.7 m (EUR 19.7 m) of which EUR 24.1 m (EUR 19.8 m) is attributable to owners of the parent. Net profit EUR 24.7 m (EUR 30.8 m) compared to Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Profit attributable to the parent’s shareholders was EUR 24.1 million, and earnings per share were EUR 0.07, compared with EUR 0.09 a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: of which EUR 24.1 m (EUR 19.8 m) is attributable to owners of the parent. Earnings per share EUR 0.07 (EUR 0.06) compared to Q1 2026 and EUR 0.07 (EUR 0.09) compared to Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: First-half net profit reached EUR 44.4 million, 26% below the EUR 59.9 million reported for the first half of 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit for the reporting period EUR 24,687 thousand (44.375 million) for Q2 2026 and EUR 30,765 thousand (30.765 million) for Q2 2025. First-half 2026 net profit was EUR 44.375 million vs EUR 59.925 million in first half 2025, a 25.9% decrease.

factual_claims.claim: Revenue performance improved during the quarter.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s net income increased by 7.3% in Q2 2026 compared to Q1 2026, amounting to EUR 79 million (EUR 73.7 million in Q1 2026). Net interest income grew by 5% in Q2 2026 compared to Q1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Net income rose 7.3% quarter-on-quarter and 7% year-on-year to EUR 79.0 million, supported primarily by net interest income, which increased 5% from Q1 to EUR 62.5 million and 8% from Q2 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net income EUR 79.0 m (EUR 73.7 m) quarter-on-quarter (7.3% increase) and EUR 79.0 m (EUR 73.9 m) year-on-year (7% increase). Net interest income grew by 5% in Q2 2026 compared to Q1 2026, amounting to EUR 62.5 million (EUR 59.3 million in Q1 2026). The Group’s net interest income grew by 8% compared to Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Net fee and commission income was broadly unchanged from Q1 at EUR 14.6 million but declined 6% year-on-year, reflecting lower client activity.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net service fee income remained at the same level as in the previous quarter, amounting to EUR 14.6 million (EUR 14.7 million in Q1 2026). Net fee and commission income for Q2 2026 was EUR 14.64 million vs EUR 15.58 million in Q2 2025, a 6% decrease.

factual_claims.claim: Net insurance income recovered to EUR 0.7 million from a EUR 0.7 million loss in Q1.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net insurance income recovered to EUR 0.7 million from the loss incurred in the previous quarter. Net insurance income for Q2 2026 was EUR 0.74 million vs a loss of EUR 0.69 million in Q1 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Operating expenses fell 4% quarter-on-quarter to EUR 43.6 million, but were 8% higher year-on-year, contributing to a cost/income ratio of 61.9%, compared with 47.3% a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses amounted to EUR 43.6 million in Q2, having decreased by EUR 2 million compared to Q1 2026 and grown by EUR 3.1 million compared to Q2 2025. Cost/income ratio was 61.9% in Q2 2026 vs 47.3% in Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: The main factor limiting profitability was a sharp increase in impairment charges.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Write-downs were increased by EUR 5.8 million in Q2 (an increase of EUR 1.3 million in Q1 2026). Loan impairment charges increased by 5.6 million during the quarter, reflecting a limited number of individual cases and higher forward-looking model provisions.

factual_claims.claim: Loan and bond portfolio losses were EUR 5.8 million in Q2, compared with EUR 1.3 million in Q1 and a EUR 4.2 million gain in Q2 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Loan and bond provisions EUR 5.8 m (EUR 1.3 m) for Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026. Loan and bond provisions EUR 5.8 m (EUR -4.2 m) for Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Management said the charges reflected forward-looking model provisions and a limited number of specific client cases, while overall loan portfolio quality remained strong and some losses were not expected to materialize.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: We applied model-based, forward-looking impairment charges for specific clients, even though we do not anticipate these losses actually materializing. Loan portfolio quality remains strong.

factual_claims.claim: Income tax expense declined to EUR 5.0 million from EUR 7.1 million in Q1 and EUR 6.8 million a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Income tax expenses EUR 5.0 m (EUR 7.1 m) for Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026. Income tax expenses EUR 5.0 m (EUR 6.8 m) for Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Business volumes continued to expand.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s loan volume grew to EUR 5,768 million by the end of Q2 (EUR 5,585 million in Q1 2026), having grown by 3% or EUR 183 million in a quarter. The volume of deposits of ordinary clients increased by EUR 105 million.

factual_claims.claim: The Group’s loan portfolio grew 3% quarter-on-quarter and 15% year-on-year to EUR 5.8 billion, while customer deposits fell 3% from Q1 to EUR 7.6 billion, mainly because of reduced platform and financial-intermediary deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s loan volume grew to EUR 5,768 million by the end of Q2 (EUR 5,585 million in Q1 2026), having grown by 3% or EUR 183 million in a quarter and by 15% compared to Q2 2025. The volume of deposits decreased by EUR 245 million in a quarter to EUR 7,557,266 thousand (7.6 billion), mainly due to reduced platform and financial-intermediary deposits.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Pank generated EUR 24.3 million of quarterly profit, up 20% from Q1 but down 18% year-on-year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Bank’s Q2 profit amounted to EUR 24.3 million, which is 20% more than in Q1 2026 (20.2) and 18% less than in Q2 2025 (29.7).

factual_claims.claim: Its loan book increased by EUR 114 million, while deposits declined by EUR 312 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Bank’s loan portfolio grew by EUR 114 million in Q2 (EUR 24 million in Q1 2026), reaching EUR 4,821 million. The volume of deposits at the Bank decreased by EUR 312 million from the previous quarter and stood at EUR 6,226 million at the end of the quarter.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Bank’s profit rose to EUR 1.4 million, and LHV Kindlustus returned to a EUR 0.8 million profit from a Q1 loss, aided by fewer major losses and lower loss frequency.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit £1.40 m vs plan of £1.25 m, a shortfall of around 10% (interpreted as EUR 1.4 million in context). LHV Kindlustus: The company’s profit in Q2 was EUR 789 thousand. The quarterly loss frequency of insurance products decreased minimally from the previous quarter and the average loss amounts also decreased, which primarily indicates the small number of major losses.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Varahaldus earned EUR 0.4 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Net profit for Q2 was EUR 0.4 million.

factual_claims.claim: Return on equity improved to 13.1% from 10.7% in Q1 but remained below 17.4% a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The return on equity owned by LHV’s shareholders was 13.1% in Q2 2026, which was 2.4 percentage points higher than in Q1 2026 (10.7%) and 4.3 percentage points lower than in Q2 2025 (17.4%).

factual_claims.claim: Capital adequacy was 20.8%, down from 23.0% year-on-year, as risk-weighted assets increased.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Capital adequacy 20.8% (23.0%) compared to Q2 2025. Risk-weighted assets increased from 3,800,198 thousand to 4,181,335 thousand.

factual_claims.claim: The quarter also included strategic changes at LHV Pank, including migration of core systems to Amazon Web Services, adoption of product-based management, and receipt of Estonia’s first bank licence for regulated crypto-asset services under MiCA.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The most important technological event of the quarter was the successful transition of the Bank’s core systems to the Amazon Web Services cloud environment. The Bank transitioned to a product-based management model in Q2. The Financial Supervision and Resolution Authority issued LHV Pank a crypto-assets service provider license under the MiCA Regulation in Q2. LHV was the first bank in Estonia to receive such a license.
